title: Intermediate Microeconomics

notes: MIT 14.04 assumes introductory micro and multivariable calculus; linear algebra, statistics, econometrics, and computing help. Some advanced applications in this offering should be optional extensions, not universal intermediate requirements.

title: Intermediate Microeconomics / Mathematical Track
level: Berkeley 101A covers similar topics to 100A with more calculus
notes: Berkeley 101A covers similar topics to 100A with more calculus. This supports a mathematical-depth setting inside the general course, rather than duplicated institution-specific courses.

level: Berkeley first-year PhD core assumes advanced undergraduate micro and ECON 204 or equivalent
notes: Berkeley first-year PhD core assumes advanced undergraduate micro and ECON 204 or equivalent. Emphasizes theorems/proofs and applying tools to new problems. Its own syllabus explicitly disclaims exhaustive coverage.

level: Graduate core; intermediate micro, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and basic real analysis
notes: Graduate core; intermediate micro, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and basic real analysis. Add formal reasoning, counterexamples, and assumption diagnosis rather than only numerical substitutions.

notes: Graduate edition requires consumer optimization and game theory. Introductory behavioral examples can share concept tags without sharing a difficulty scale.

title: Principles of Macroeconomics
level: Introductory undergraduate
notes: Platform recommendation: arithmetic, percentages, graphs; do not infer a calculus requirement from the topic list.

title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
level: Undergraduate
topics: Solow, golden rule, human capital, convergence and growth accounting
endogenous growth, learning, R&D and biased technical change
permanent income, borrowing constraints and investment Q
notes: MIT explicitly requires principles of micro and macro. Columbia explicitly requires principles and Calculus I; recommends Calculus III and intermediate micro. Platform should tag calculus/ODE depth rather than treating all intermediate courses identically.

title: Advanced Macroeconomic Theory
level: Graduate core / advanced undergraduate bridge selected by mathematical readiness
topics: RBC calibration, factor utilization and model evaluation
notes: Platform recommendation: intermediate theory, multivariable calculus, optimization, probability, difference equations. The graduate source is not evidence that all these belong in ordinary undergraduate intermediate macro.

title: Economic Growth and Development
level: Advanced undergraduate conceptual track; separate graduate mathematical track
topics: endogenous innovation, expanding varieties and quality ladders
technical change and distribution. Separate proximate accounting from causal institutional explanations
notes: Platform recommendation: intermediate macro; graduate derivations additionally need dynamic optimization and general equilibrium.

title: Monetary Economics and Stabilization Policy
level: Upper undergraduate foundations; separate graduate policy track
notes: MIT advanced offering explicitly requires graduate microeconomic theory and economic growth. Platform: introduce policy rules and transmission before optimal-policy derivations.

title: International Macroeconomics
level: Upper undergraduate / MA
topics: terms of trade and world interest rate
nominal rigidity, currency pegs and balance-of-payments crises
notes: Platform recommendation: intermediate macro, intertemporal budgets, basic optimization. Source explicitly labels its materials BA/MA.

title: Open-Economy Macroeconomic Theory
level: Graduate core
topics: open-economy RBC calibration, approximation and stationarity
interest-rate shocks. Terms of trade, nontradables, nominal rigidity, controls, credibility, financial frictions and sovereign default are explicitly time-permitting extensions in this syllabus
notes: First-year PhD sequence; platform recommendation: dynamic stochastic optimization and prior graduate macro.

title: Financial Crises and International Macro Policy
level: Graduate field
topics: nominal wage rigidity, currency pegs and unemployment
notes: Platform recommendation: graduate macro, open-economy models, numerical methods; scaffold conceptual questions separately.

title: Empirical Macroeconomics and Monetary History
